title: Secrets in Git/artifacts
overview: Triage a secret-scanner finding based on its classification and artifact exposure.
prerequisites: Read the baseline and compare event fields. No external tools are required.

attack.name: Credentials In Files
attack.rationale: Credentials in Files models discovery of credentials in files. The lab detects potential exposure only.

hypothesis: A credential-like finding in a shared artifact merits checking ownership and publication scope.
evidence: Read scanner rule, path and exposure. Preserve only redacted findings and check whether the artifact was distributed.
false_positive: Documentation placeholders and test strings commonly match scanner patterns.
tuning: Allowlist exact, reviewed examples with safe meaning and location. Leave generic formats covered.
response: Verify the finding privately, revoke or rotate a real credential if confirmed, and scope any access after disclosure.
prevention: Run secret scanning before release and use short-lived credentials or workload identity.
validation: Baseline and noisy fixture produce no alerts. The positive fixture produces an alert with linked evidence.
limitations: The fixture contains an inert scanner label. No secret or token-looking value is included.

questions.prompt: What should be shared in a report?
options: The redacted finding and affected path
questions.explanation: Redacted metadata supports triage without exposing a credential.

options: Distribution or exposure of the artifact
questions.explanation: Sharing increases who can access a valid credential.
